subject.title: Durable Core PR 4/6: persist agent-turn front doors

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `durable.mode` and the shared SQLite durable-runtime/recovery layer as a supported core product contract, rather than keeping durability out of core until a narrower owner-approved design exists?
rationale: The patch is not a narrow repair: it introduces persistent state, a new top-level configuration family, recovery-worker behavior, and fail-closed fallback semantics. Repository policy makes those maintainer product and compatibility decisions rather than contributor-resolvable implementation details.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core durable contract
options.body: Approve the durable config, shared-state schema, authority-mode behavior, and explicit upgrade proof requirements, then review the implementation against that accepted boundary.

options.title: Defer core adoption
options.body: Keep the PR unmerged until maintainers define a narrower durable-runtime roadmap or decide that the capability should not become a core contract.

options.title: Narrow to an accepted seam
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that uses an existing owner/plugin boundary and avoids introducing the new core config and durable database contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded core durable contract
recommendation.body: Approve the durable config, shared-state schema, authority-mode behavior, and explicit upgrade proof requirements, then review the implementation against that accepted boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor can clarify the stack boundary and revise the proposal, while a repository owner must make the final sponsorship decision.
